all: Give every controlled device a DHCP reservation (or static IP outside the pool) before adding it in Composer.
Wire it if it has an Ethernet port. Several TVs only wake over LAN (Wake-on-LAN) when wired.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on TVs, AVRs and sources unless the driver needs it. CEC fights the control system (inputs and power changing on their own).
Set network/IP standby to the 'always on' option so the device can be turned on over IP. It uses a little more standby power.
Turn off eco / auto power off / auto standby timers so devices don't sleep or drop off the network behind Control4's back.
Turn on Control4 SDDP where the device offers it (Epson, JVC, LG, Sonos) so the driver follows IP changes.
Note the MAC address and any pairing key or password in the site network map, never in the driver notes.
After a firmware update, re-check these settings. Updates have reset them before (Roku network access, Samsung pairing).

sky_q.title: Sky Q and Sky Q Mini
c4: Power: set standby to Active, not Eco. In Eco the box drops off the network overnight and stops answering IP control. Path: Home > Settings > Setup > Preferences > Power (path from the Remotes README, wording differs by firmware).
HDMI control (CEC): Home > Settings > Setup > Audio visual > HDMI control > Off, so the box can't switch the TV on or change inputs after its nightly reboot.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on the TV too. Sky forum Superusers note the TV's own CEC and 'auto switch to active HDMI' settings also cause wake-ups at night.
Give each box a DHCP reservation. IP control is TCP 49160 (keys) and HTTP 9006 (status).

Installer menu also has Network (Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz, Powerline, Ethernet on/off), Reset (settings / factory) and Apps > Refresh apps. Turn off Wi-Fi/Powerline on wired rack boxes if you want them on Ethernet only.
Unverified, check on the model: Sky Q Mini uses the same installer route as the main box; no source covered the Mini specifically.

installer.title: Sky Q installer menu
steps: Scroll down to Settings and highlight it. Do not press Select.
The installer menu opens (Network, Reset, Apps).

tasks.text: Power: set standby to Active, not Eco. In Eco the box drops off the network overnight and stops answering IP control. Path: Home > Settings > Setup > Preferences > Power (path from the Remotes README, wording differs by firmware).
HDMI control (CEC): Home > Settings > Setup > Audio visual > HDMI control > Off, so the box can't switch the TV on or change inputs after its nightly reboot.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on the TV too. Sky forum Superusers note the TV's own CEC and 'auto switch to active HDMI' settings also cause wake-ups at night.
Give each box a DHCP reservation. IP control is TCP 49160 (keys) and HTTP 9006 (status).

Installer menu also has Network (Wi-Fi 2.4/5GHz, Powerline, Ethernet on/off), Reset (settings / factory) and Apps > Refresh apps. Turn off Wi-Fi/Powerline on wired rack boxes if you want them on Ethernet only.
Sky Q Mini uses the same installer route as the main box; no source covered the Mini specifically.

issues.title: Sky Q shows offline after firmware moved the IP control port to 49160
issues.symptom: Sky Q IP driver shows the box offline and commands do nothing, even though the box's IP address is correct.
issues.fix: Use a maintained driver (Chowmain Sky driver), or set the driver port to 49160. Older free drivers used 5900.
issues.detail: Firmware Q060.000.28.00L (Dec 2017) moved remote control from 5900 to 49160; Chowmain fixed it on 2 Dec 2017. Status/JSON API is 9006. Intrinsic's drivers use an unofficial API Sky hasn't published.

issues.title: Eco standby makes boxes unreachable about 02:45 to 05:45
issues.symptom: Sky Q main and multiroom boxes show 'not connected' or ignore control in the early hours, then work again from about 06:00.
issues.fix: Home > Settings > Setup > Preferences: set Standby mode to Active (or None) instead of Eco.
issues.detail: Sky forum accepted answer: Eco runs low power 2:45am to 5:45am. Moving Eco to Active did not stop an overnight TV wake for one poster (that is CEC, see next).

issues.title: Overnight reboot wakes the TV or AV receiver through HDMI-CEC
issues.symptom: TV or AVR turns on between about 1am and 4am, or every morning after the Sky Q overnight reset.
issues.fix: On the Sky Q: Home > Settings > Setup > Audio visual > HDMI control > Off, and turn CEC off on the TV and AVR too.
issues.detail: Mixed results: fixed it for some, not others. The TV's 'auto switch to active HDMI' can be the trigger. With an Onkyo TX-NR676E, HDMI control off caused input flipping; that poster set AVR auto-standby to 30 min instead.

issues.title: Wired Sky Q multiroom creates switching loops or STP blocking
issues.symptom: With the main box and Minis all on Ethernet, the LAN slows badly (550 to 24 Mbps in one report), switch ports flap or block (UniFi), Minis drop out.
issues.fix: Turn off both Wi-Fi bands on every wired box in the installer menu (Home, highlight Settings, 0 0 1 Select > Network) after a wired network reset.
issues.detail: The boxes' AirTies mesh bridges Wi-Fi and Ethernet at the same time. One poster's only working setup was Q and Minis on their own switch with a single uplink to the router. Sky says managed switches can cause problems.

issues.title: Q Minis drop out on managed networks (IGMP snooping, WIPS)
issues.symptom: Q Minis lose the main box, often overnight, on Meraki or other managed networks; ports flap and APs report disassociation.
issues.fix: Hardwire the boxes. If it continues, disable IGMP snooping on the switches carrying Sky Q, and whitelist the Sky mesh in wireless intrusion prevention.
issues.detail: IGMP snooping fix is from a single poster. Another found the main box's DHCP blocked until whitelisted.

issues.title: A separate VLAN for Sky Q doesn't reliably help
issues.symptom: Wired Minis still lose the main box for minutes at a time on a managed L3 network; on another job a dedicated VLAN gave 'no internet' on the Q home screen.
issues.fix: Keep the Sky Q main box and Minis on simple unmanaged switching to the router rather than a VLAN over managed switches, with Wi-Fi off on all boxes.
issues.detail: Secondhand report that Sky support says VLANs aren't supported on older Q boxes. No confirmed fix in either thread.

issues.title: Minis lose connection after a firmware update
issues.symptom: After a firmware update Minis lose connection over Wi-Fi and Ethernet; one main box froze with high fan speed.
issues.fix: Reboot the main box then the Minis, network-reset and re-pair each Mini, and move the site's 5 GHz APs off channels 36 to 48 (the Q mesh default).
issues.detail: Channel 36-48 explanation is one poster's suggestion, not confirmed.

issues.title: IR fallback works alongside the Bluetooth remote
issues.symptom: Worry that Control4 IR will conflict with the client's Bluetooth Sky Q remote, or Sky+HD IR codes tried on a Q box.
issues.fix: Use a Sky Q-specific IR code set; the box takes IR and Bluetooth at once, so the client's remote stays paired.
issues.detail: Sky Q and Q Mini share IR codes; Sky+HD codes don't work on Q. On a Sky Q remote: 4+6 = IR mode, 1+3 = re-pair Bluetooth, 7+9 = reset.

issues.title: Chowmain Sky driver: Guide and Pause mapping
issues.symptom: Guide does nothing on Sky Q, or Pause behaves wrongly, with the Chowmain driver.
issues.fix: Map Guide to HOME (not TVGUIDE) on Sky Q, and set the driver's Pause property to 'Play/Pause' for Sky Q.
issues.detail: Supports Sky+HD, Q, Q Silver, Q Mini. Needs OS 2.6+ and the driverCentral licensing driver. 24 Aug 2022 update fixed timer leaks on OS 2.10.x, so update old installs.

issues.title: Box lockups: program on the driver's offline event
issues.symptom: Sky boxes occasionally lock up and need a power cycle, causing service calls.
issues.fix: Program against the Chowmain driver's Connection Status offline event, with a switchable power outlet to power-cycle the box.
issues.detail: Driver retries every minute and fires offline after 5 failures. Developer suggested remote monitoring (Domotz) plus a smart plug.

issues.title: Matrix video: duplicate events and no sync on power-on
issues.symptom: Sky commands fire more than once in distributed video; no picture after power-on through a matrix.
issues.fix: Update the Chowmain driver (29 Mar 2020 or later) and set its power-on delay so the HDMI chain can sync.
issues.detail: Changelog also fixed Sky+HD extra commands in matrixed systems (Mar 2017) and STOP not sent from remotes on poor Wi-Fi/Zigbee (Jan 2021).

sky_hd.title: Sky+HD
c4: Check the box is actually on the network (Services > Settings > Network). Most Sky+HD boxes were installed without a cable, and IP control (TCP 5900) needs one.
Give it a DHCP reservation. There is no status API, so Control4 can't read power state; use IR or a video/current sense if you need it.

Installer menu is mainly used for the RF outlet: turn RF outlet power on, set the channel (default CH68; some amplifiers only tune to CH60), press Green to save. It also holds LNB settings for single-feed installs.
Unverified, check on the model: Some guides give Select, 0 0 1, Select instead of Services first. Try that if Services doesn't work.

installer.title: Sky+HD installer menu
steps: Press 0 0 1 then Select (newer guide). The digits don't show on screen; that's normal.
On the old guide the sequence is Services, 4, 0 1, Select.
For the RF outlet: open RF outlets, set RF outlet power supply to On, press Green to save.

tasks.text: Check the box is actually on the network (Services > Settings > Network). Most Sky+HD boxes were installed without a cable, and IP control (TCP 5900) needs one.
Give it a DHCP reservation. There is no status API, so Control4 can't read power state; use IR or a video/current sense if you need it.

Installer menu is mainly used for the RF outlet: turn RF outlet power on, set the channel (default CH68; some amplifiers only tune to CH60), press Green to save. It also holds LNB settings for single-feed installs.
Some guides give Select, 0 0 1, Select instead of Services first. Try that if Services doesn't work.

issues.title: Sky+HD power-cycles when selected from another room (Pulse-Eight driver)
issues.symptom: With the Pulse-Eight Sky HD IP driver, the box powers off and on when users switch to it from different rooms.
issues.fix: In Composer set the Pulse-Eight Sky HD IP driver property 'Allow Power Off' to Off.
issues.detail: Pulse-Eight knowledge base article.

issues.title: Pause starts playback after a driver update
issues.symptom: Pressing Pause on a Control4 remote starts playback on Sky+HD.
issues.fix: In the Chowmain driver set the Pause property to 'Pause' (Sky+HD), not 'Play/Pause'.
issues.detail: Default reverted to Pause in Aug 2020.

sky_stream.title: Sky Stream and Sky Glass
c4: There is no installer menu on Stream or Glass (Sky forum Superuser answer; 0 0 1 Select only opens Retail mode).
To refresh apps: Settings > System > Apps & updates > Refresh apps.
IP control needs a third-party driver (Chowmain Sky driver) or IR into the puck's IR window. Give the puck a DHCP reservation.
Unverified, check on the model: turn HDMI-CEC off on the TV if the puck switches the TV on or changes inputs.

tasks.text: There is no installer menu on Stream or Glass (Sky forum Superuser answer; 0 0 1 Select only opens Retail mode).
To refresh apps: Settings > System > Apps & updates > Refresh apps.
IP control needs a third-party driver (Chowmain Sky driver) or IR into the puck's IR window. Give the puck a DHCP reservation.
turn HDMI-CEC off on the TV if the puck switches the TV on or changes inputs.

issues.title: Stream and Glass were IR only (no open API)
issues.symptom: No Control4 IP driver for the puck or Glass; CEC attempts failed.
issues.fix: Control the puck by IR with an emitter on its IR window (community IR driver on c4forums or a learned code set), unless using the newer Chowmain IP driver.
issues.detail: 2023: Chowmain said the puck had no open ports or API. Wake-on-LAN packets repeatedly crashed one user's pucks. Ping-based power detection is unreliable.

issues.title: Chowmain Sky Stream IP driver (July 2026): keep IR for power-on on older pucks
issues.symptom: With IP control, some earlier pucks don't wake reliably over the network.
issues.fix: Update the Chowmain Sky driver and use IP control, but keep an IR emitter for power-on on older pucks.
issues.detail: From a trade-news podcast summary (8 Jul 2026), not Chowmain's own notes. Check driverCentral before quoting it.

issues.title: Puck wakes from deep sleep only by IR line of sight
issues.symptom: A puck in a cupboard won't power on unless the remote points at it; once awake the Bluetooth remote works out of sight.
issues.fix: Fit an IR emitter on the puck's IR window for the wake command.
issues.detail: Also turn Network standby on and overnight power saving off in Start Up and Standby settings; deep sleep still happened for one user with those set.

issues.title: Power is a toggle, so IR macros drift out of sync
issues.symptom: A power-on sent while the puck is slow to start turns it back off.
issues.fix: Use HOME as the 'on' command in the IR driver and keep Power (toggle) only for standby.
issues.detail: Home didn't wake every user's puck.

lg.title: LG webOS TV
c4: Use the IR remote (not the Magic/pointer remote) for the installer codes.
Turn off energy saving settings under All Settings, or the TV may not power on from cold.
TV on with mobile: Settings > General > Devices > External devices > TV on with mobile > Turn on via Wi-Fi > On. Snap One says this must be on even when wired.
IP Control Setup (see installer) > SDDP > On.
IP Control Setup > Wake-on-LAN > On.
IP Control Setup > Network IP Control > On.
IP Control Setup > Generate Keycode, and record the key in the network map. A new keycode invalidates the old one.
Once IP control is set, Wake-on-LAN is the only way to turn the TV on from standby, so wire it and note its MAC.
Static IP or DHCP reservation, wired.
Unverified, check on the model: turn SimpLink (HDMI-CEC) off: Settings > General > Devices > HDMI Settings > SimpLink (HDMI-CEC). Path varies by webOS version.

installer.title: LG IP Control Settings
steps: 2026 and later: Settings > Support > IP Control Settings.
Older: Settings > All Settings > General > Network. Highlight Network, don't press OK, then key 8 2 8 8 8 quickly. IP Control Setup appears after a few seconds.
If that fails, some models take 7 3 7 7 7 on the Network icon.
Fallback installer menu: go to a CATV input showing snow, hold Settings until the channel number shows, then 8 2 8 OK (or 1 1 0 5) and set IP control On.

tasks.text: Use the IR remote (not the Magic/pointer remote) for the installer codes.
Turn off energy saving settings under All Settings, or the TV may not power on from cold.
TV on with mobile: Settings > General > Devices > External devices > TV on with mobile > Turn on via Wi-Fi > On. Snap One says this must be on even when wired.
IP Control Setup (see installer) > SDDP > On.
IP Control Setup > Wake-on-LAN > On.
IP Control Setup > Network IP Control > On.
IP Control Setup > Generate Keycode, and record the key in the network map. A new keycode invalidates the old one.
Once IP control is set, Wake-on-LAN is the only way to turn the TV on from standby, so wire it and note its MAC.
Static IP or DHCP reservation, wired.
turn SimpLink (HDMI-CEC) off: Settings > General > Devices > HDMI Settings > SimpLink (HDMI-CEC). Path varies by webOS version.

issues.title: IP control not enabled in the installer menu
issues.symptom: Driver never connects; 'Connected to Network' stays false and Get MAC fails.
issues.fix: With the IR remote, open IP Control Setup (8 2 8 8 8 on highlighted Network), set Network IP Control and SDDP On, generate the keycode and put it in the driver's Password property.
issues.detail: If the pointer moves while typing, the code fails. 2021 sets may need 7 3 7 7 7 or the CATV snow method; some 2021 OLEDs couldn't reach it at all. Keycode can be read only once.

issues.title: Won't turn on over IP: Mobile TV On off
issues.symptom: TV turns off from Control4 but won't turn back on.
issues.fix: Settings > General > Mobile TV On > Turn on via Wi-Fi > On (needed even when wired).
issues.detail: Driver docs also ask for Wake on LAN, Always Ready and a DHCP reservation.

issues.title: Quick Start+ off: 30 s dead period after power-on
issues.symptom: TV powers on but ignores the input command for ~30 s (2022 G2).
issues.fix: Turn Quick Start+ On (webOS 23+: General > System > Additional Settings; webOS 22: General > Devices > TV Management; older: General).
issues.detail: Also enable the driver's input delay timer (~2000 ms). Uses a little standby power.

issues.title: Turns on once, then won't wake (or stops after a reset)
issues.symptom: Power-on works after adding the driver, but once off, WoL no longer wakes it.
issues.fix: After any factory reset or mains power cut, re-check Quick Start+, LivePlus and Mobile TV On.
issues.detail: One poster has to power the TVs with the LG remote after a mains cut before Control4 works again.

issues.title: WoL fails on wired: wrong MAC or crossing subnets
issues.symptom: TV wakes over Wi-Fi but not Ethernet.
issues.fix: Put the TV's wired MAC in the driver (it had kept the Wi-Fi MAC) and keep the TV on the controller's subnet.
issues.detail: Controller sends WoL to 255.255.255.255 UDP 9; blocked by routers/firewalls in between.

issues.title: Wi-Fi-only connection is laggy and unreliable
issues.symptom: ~2 s lag, apps don't launch, On fails after hours off.
issues.fix: Hard-wire the TV and delete the Wi-Fi network from it, then re-enter the MAC/IP and re-pair the driver.

issues.title: OLED pixel refresh needs mains power after switch-off
issues.symptom: Cutting power at room off (switched outlet/relay) stops the OLED compensation cycle.
issues.fix: Never cut mains to LG OLEDs as part of room off; leave them in standby.
issues.detail: LG: pixel cleaning won't run if unplugged; the 2,000-hour run takes about an hour.

issues.title: SimpLink (HDMI-CEC) fights Control4 power
issues.symptom: TV turns on/off by itself or fails to turn off from Control4.
issues.fix: Turn SimpLink off (webOS 22: General > Devices > HDMI Settings > SimpLink (HDMI-CEC); 2020: Connection > Device Connection Settings; 2019: Connection > HDMI Device Settings).
issues.detail: Also check the Power On Timer.

issues.title: Firmware update clears IP pairing: add IR fallback
issues.symptom: Network control stops after a TV update clears the pairing.
issues.fix: In the McGlothlin LG WebOS driver set IR Setting to 'IR WOL Fallback' (or RS-232) with an emitter on the TV.
issues.detail: Sends backup power-on if no response in 8 s. Apps still need network.

issues.title: Changes made outside Control4 aren't seen
issues.symptom: Programming on TV on/off doesn't fire when the TV's own remote or AirPlay is used.
issues.fix: Wire the TV's USB port (5 V when on) to a controller contact input and trigger from that.

issues.title: Toast notifications unpair older webOS
issues.symptom: Sending a toast unpaired a webOS 4.1 TV; icon toasts fail on 4.5.
issues.fix: Send text-only toasts, or turn toast programming off on affected TVs.

samsung.title: Samsung Tizen TV
c4: IP Remote: Settings > All Settings > Connection > Network > Expert Settings > IP Remote > Enable (2021 and older: Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings).
Power On with Mobile: same Expert Settings menu > Power On with Mobile > On.
Wire it so Wake-on-LAN works. After the TV has been off for over a minute its IP server is offline, so Control4 needs WoL; send both IP power-on and WoL.
Record the MAC: Settings > Support > About This TV > Wired MAC Address. Samsung calls a wrong MAC the most common cause of failed power-on.
Pairing: when Control4 first connects, a prompt appears on the TV. Press Allow with the TV remote (TV must be on).
Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) Off: Samsung says control partners ask for this because CEC can disrupt communication and reliable control.
Eco settings: Samsung says these can affect timing and reliability. Turn off auto power off / eco timers.
Far-field voice models: keeping Bixby in standby (Settings > General > Voice > Voice Assistant > Bixby Wakeup Options) may keep the IP server open.
Static IP via DHCP reservation.

installer.title: Samsung HDMI Auto Detect toggle
steps: Turn the TV on, set Source to TV.
IR remote: Mute, 7 2 9, Exit. Smart remote: Mute, Vol down, Ch down, Mute.
No message appears. Entering it again turns it back on. Disabling HDMI Auto Detect stops inputs switching on their own.

tasks.text: IP Remote: Settings > All Settings > Connection > Network > Expert Settings > IP Remote > Enable (2021 and older: Settings > General > Network > Expert Settings).
Power On with Mobile: same Expert Settings menu > Power On with Mobile > On.
Wire it so Wake-on-LAN works. After the TV has been off for over a minute its IP server is offline, so Control4 needs WoL; send both IP power-on and WoL.
Record the MAC: Settings > Support > About This TV > Wired MAC Address. Samsung calls a wrong MAC the most common cause of failed power-on.
Pairing: when Control4 first connects, a prompt appears on the TV. Press Allow with the TV remote (TV must be on).
Anynet+ (HDMI-CEC) Off: Samsung says control partners ask for this because CEC can disrupt communication and reliable control.
Eco settings: Samsung says these can affect timing and reliability. Turn off auto power off / eco timers.
Far-field voice models: keeping Bixby in standby (Settings > General > Voice > Voice Assistant > Bixby Wakeup Options) may keep the IP server open.
Static IP via DHCP reservation.

issues.title: IP Remote and Power On with Mobile must both be on
issues.symptom: Driver controls the TV but won't power it on, or won't pair.
issues.fix: Connection > Network > Expert Settings: IP Remote = Enable and Power On With Mobile = On (2021 and older: General > Network > Expert Settings).
issues.detail: Drivers split 2019-and-earlier vs 2020-and-later (port change). Wire for WoL.

issues.title: No 'Allow' prompt when pairing
issues.symptom: Pair with TV shows no pop-up, or control is lost later.
issues.fix: With the TV on, toggle IP Remote off/on, delete old paired devices (or factory reset), pair again and press Allow on the Samsung remote.
issues.detail: Some EU models up to 2021 never show the prompt.

issues.title: Wrong MAC in the driver breaks WoL
issues.symptom: Power-on fails after the TV has been off a while.
issues.fix: Read the MAC at Settings > Support > About This TV and enter it by hand in the driver.
issues.detail: After ~1 minute off, only WoL wakes it, so send both IP power-on and WoL.

issues.title: Frame: Art Mode or full off at room off
issues.symptom: Room Off sends the Frame to Art Mode, too bright in bedrooms.
issues.fix: Set the driver's 'On Power Off' property to Power Off or Art Mode to suit the room.
issues.detail: Can be changed on a schedule by programming the property, then on then off.

issues.title: Frame won't power on from full off
issues.symptom: Fully off Frame stops answering ping/WoL; reliable only from Art Mode.
issues.fix: Add the Frame by DHCP reservation/IP rather than SDDP, and power off to Art Mode.
issues.detail: No confirmed fix; consider RS-232/IR for power.

issues.title: Frame unresponsive in the morning (SDDP unknown-Mac)
issues.symptom: Control4 shows Art Mode but the screen is black and commands are ignored.
issues.fix: Change the driver from SDDP to IP identification with a DHCP reservation.
issues.detail: Also: driver retry count above 4, turn off the TV's Night Mode if Sleep After is used.

issues.title: Frame Art Mode mini-driver
issues.symptom: Art Mode missing from Watch, or the mini-app rarely works.
issues.fix: Install the Samsung Art Mode mini driver in the same room, connect it, then Refresh Navigators.
issues.detail: Driver doesn't expose the Frame's motion sensor; use a separate sensor. Programmed Art Mode is more reliable than the mini-app.

issues.title: EU/UK models without IP Remote
issues.symptom: Expert Settings > IP Remote missing, or no driver for a QE-prefix model.
issues.fix: Update the TV firmware; if IP Remote is still missing, use RS-232 (ex-link) or IR.
issues.detail: QE/UE = EU, QN/UN = US. Newer One Connect boxes may lack ex-link.

issues.title: SDDP discovery fails on some models
issues.symptom: TV never appears in Discovered Devices.
issues.fix: Add the driver by hand with a DHCP reservation and the correct MAC.

issues.title: Cutting mains power with a switched outlet
issues.symptom: Installers cut power to a Frame/One Connect at night to force a clean off.
issues.fix: Avoid routine power cuts; if you must, turn off TV auto-updates first.
issues.detail: Risk of corruption during firmware writes.

sony.title: Sony Bravia TV
c4: IP control authentication: Settings > Network & Internet > Home network > IP control > Authentication > Normal and Pre-Shared Key, then set the key and enter the same key in the Control4 driver.
Remote device control: Settings > Network & Internet > Remote device settings > Control remotely > On. This also enables Wake-on-LAN.
If the TV suspends, its web server stops and IP control won't answer until WoL powers it back. Wire it and note the MAC.
DHCP reservation, wired.
Unverified, check on the model: turn Bravia Sync (HDMI-CEC) off: Settings > Channels & Inputs > External inputs > BRAVIA Sync settings > BRAVIA Sync control. Path varies by year.
Unverified, check on the model: older (pre-Google TV) menus call it 'Remote start' (Settings > Network > Remote start > On) and 'Simple IP control'.

tasks.text: IP control authentication: Settings > Network & Internet > Home network > IP control > Authentication > Normal and Pre-Shared Key, then set the key and enter the same key in the Control4 driver.
Remote device control: Settings > Network & Internet > Remote device settings > Control remotely > On. This also enables Wake-on-LAN.
If the TV suspends, its web server stops and IP control won't answer until WoL powers it back. Wire it and note the MAC.
DHCP reservation, wired.
turn Bravia Sync (HDMI-CEC) off: Settings > Channels & Inputs > External inputs > BRAVIA Sync settings > BRAVIA Sync control. Path varies by year.
older (pre-Google TV) menus call it 'Remote start' (Settings > Network > Remote start > On) and 'Simple IP control'.

issues.title: Pre-shared key lost after reset or update
issues.symptom: After a reset or update Control4 can't control the TV.
issues.fix: Re-set IP control Authentication = Pre-Shared Key with the same key as the driver, and re-set the static IP.
issues.detail: Android TV path: Settings > BRAVIA Settings > IP control.

issues.title: Remote start needed for network power-on
issues.symptom: TV can't be turned on over the network.
issues.fix: Turn on Remote start (Settings > BRAVIA Settings > Remote start, or Network and Internet > Remote start).

issues.title: TV drops off the network daily (deep sleep)
issues.symptom: TV stops answering ping and won't power on; 'LAN Failed' (2021 A80J/A90J/X800H).
issues.fix: Turn Simple IP control On at the TV (Network > Home Network > IP control > Simple IP control), even if the driver uses the Web API.
issues.detail: Sony: Simple IP control prevents suspend. Helps but isn't always a cure.

issues.title: Driver network API: Simple vs Web
issues.symptom: IP control intermittent.
issues.fix: Set the Control4 Sony driver's network API to Simple; if a TV drops, toggle Web then Simple.

issues.title: IP changes despite static setting
issues.symptom: TV's IP changes and control is lost.
issues.fix: Set a static IP on the TV and a matching DHCP reservation on the router.
issues.detail: Experiences with SDDP vs IP conflict.

issues.title: Update switches Simple IP off; A95L ignores IR power-on
issues.symptom: Control stops after an update; A95L ignores discrete IR ON in deep sleep.
issues.fix: After any update, check Simple IP control and toggle it off and on.

issues.title: BRAVIA Sync / ARC turns the TV off
issues.symptom: TV powers on from Control4 then switches itself off (soundbar on ARC).
issues.fix: Turn off BRAVIA Sync / CEC, or use optical instead of ARC.

issues.title: TV turns on but won't turn off
issues.symptom: A 2023 KD-75X77CL powers on from Control4 but never turns off over IR.
issues.fix: Turn off HDMI-CEC and move the driver to IP control.
issues.detail: Unresolved in threads.

issues.title: Android BRAVIA locks up under IP control
issues.symptom: TV locks up and needs a power cycle, or knocks out the network.
issues.fix: Update the TV firmware; if it continues, control by IR and use an external streamer.

issues.title: Fallback: IR plus external streamer
issues.symptom: IP control stays unreliable on some units.
issues.fix: Control power and input by IR or serial and use an Apple TV or Roku for apps.

issues.title: EU BRAVIA Professional: Control Remotely off by default
issues.symptom: IP control doesn't respond on EU pro displays after RED-DA changes.
issues.fix: Settings > Network & Internet > Remote device settings > Control Remotely > On, then enable the Control4 item, Pre-Shared Key and Simple IP control under IP control.
issues.detail: Pro displays only, not consumer sets.

denon.title: Denon and Marantz AV receivers
c4: Network standby: Setup > Network > Network Control (older models: IP Control) > Always On. Off In Standby stops IP control when the unit is in standby. Denon notes Always On uses more standby power.
Unverified, check on the model: Setup > Video > HDMI Setup > HDMI Control > Off, unless you're relying on ARC/eARC from the TV.
Unverified, check on the model: Setup > General > ECO > Auto Standby > Off, and ECO Mode Off (or On) rather than Auto so volume/power behaviour is predictable.
DHCP reservation, wired. Marantz uses the same menus and protocol.

Setup > Video > HDMI Setup > HDMI Control > Off, unless you're relying on ARC/eARC from the TV.
Setup > General > ECO > Auto Standby > Off, and ECO Mode Off (or On) rather than Auto so volume/power behaviour is predictable.
DHCP reservation, wired. Marantz uses the same menus and protocol.

issues.title: AVR won't power on over IP from standby
issues.symptom: Control4 controls the AVR once on but can't turn it on.
issues.fix: Denon: Settings > Network > Network Control > Always On. Marantz: Settings > Network > IP Control > Always On.
issues.detail: Default on some Denons (AVC-S670H) is Off In Standby. Uses more standby power.

issues.title: Only one telnet control session at a time
issues.symptom: A second IP controller (Home Assistant, another driver or app) is refused or knocks Control4 off.
issues.fix: Make sure only the Control4 driver holds the AVR's telnet session; remove other telnet integrations to that AVR.
issues.detail: From the Home Assistant Denon integration docs, not Denon.

issues.title: Control lost after a power cut, IP change or firmware update
issues.symptom: Control4 can't power on the AVR or change volume after a power blip or update; other functions may still work.
issues.fix: Give the AVR a DHCP reservation by MAC, then power-cycle it.
issues.detail: One firmware update changed the AVR's IP setup; turning DHCP off on the AVR restored control. Workaround for on-then-off: 3 s delay before the final ON/OFF in macros.

issues.title: Online in Composer but commands do nothing
issues.symptom: AVR (X1400H) shows Online but only Connect/Disconnect work; log shows repeated poll failures.
issues.fix: Check Network Control is Always On and HDMI Control is off; if it still fails, factory-reset the AVR and add it again.
issues.detail: Factory reset fixed it for the poster.

issues.title: Volume runs away after one volume-up
issues.symptom: One volume-up keeps raising volume until the LAN cable is pulled (AVR-X2100, SR6008).
issues.fix: Give the AVR a DHCP reservation and check the network for faults.
issues.detail: Cause not confirmed; suspected network problem.

issues.title: Input jumps to CD when the AVR has two audio paths
issues.symptom: After OS 3.4, Denon zones switch from CBL/SAT to CD about 2 s after any Watch selection.
issues.fix: Fix bindings so video sources have only one audio path into the receiver, or add the AV Path Setter driver per room.
issues.detail: Seen with a video matrix to CBL/SAT plus an audio matrix to CD. Also check for leftover programming from a previous dealer.

issues.title: HEOS grouping out of sync with Control4
issues.symptom: Music plays in the wrong rooms; zones not ungrouped at room off.
issues.fix: Do all grouping from Control4, not the HEOS app.

issues.title: No volume feedback over RS-232
issues.symptom: Volume slider doesn't work on an RS-232 Denon because no level comes back.
issues.fix: Use the IP driver rather than serial where the model supports it.
issues.detail: Posters disagree on whether serial feedback broke after OS 2.10.6.

yamaha.title: Yamaha AV receivers
c4: Network Standby: Setup > Network > Network Standby > On. 'Auto' lets it go into a power-save state where it can't be turned on from the network.
Unverified, check on the model: Setup > HDMI > HDMI Control > Off.
Unverified, check on the model: Setup > ECO > Auto Power Standby > Off, ECO Mode Off.
DHCP reservation, wired. Yamaha MusicCast models also integrate with Control4 for MusicCast control.

tasks.text: Network Standby: Setup > Network > Network Standby > On. 'Auto' lets it go into a power-save state where it can't be turned on from the network.
Setup > HDMI > HDMI Control > Off.
Setup > ECO > Auto Power Standby > Off, ECO Mode Off.
DHCP reservation, wired. Yamaha MusicCast models also integrate with Control4 for MusicCast control.

issues.title: Network Standby needed for IP power-on
issues.symptom: Yamaha AVR can't be powered on over IP.
issues.fix: Setup > Network > Network Standby > On (or Auto when wired).
issues.detail: Off also disables Bluetooth standby. Auto goes power-saving if the cable is unplugged.

issues.title: Several Yamaha AVRs drop off Control4
issues.symptom: With more than one IP Yamaha, receivers keep going offline; queued keep-alives can flood the controller.
issues.fix: Keep the default control port (50000), and use RS-232 where the AVR has it.
issues.detail: Moving off 50000 caused false offline. One poster cured it by replacing a consumer router (AirPort Extreme).

issues.title: RX-A1030 loses IP control until power-cycled
issues.symptom: Receiver keeps dropping IP control until unplugged.
issues.fix: Delete the Yamaha driver from the project and add it again.
issues.detail: Others blamed a consumer router.

issues.title: Network standby stops answering after hours
issues.symptom: AVR answers ping but refuses control after hours to a day in standby; waking by hand restores it.
issues.fix: Update the AVR firmware; power-cycle if it recurs.
issues.detail: RX-A810, Home Assistant forum.

issues.title: Receiver power tied to source selection
issues.symptom: Receiver On/Off actions don't work on RX-A1010; it only powers with a source or Room Off.
issues.fix: Program zone power with the device-specific commands.
issues.detail: MAIN and ZONE2 power behave as toggles.

issues.title: No driver for custom-install TSR models
issues.symptom: TSR-7850/8750 isn't in the Control4 driver database.
issues.fix: Use the IP driver for the matching-year RX-A model (e.g. RX-A870) and add the AVR by fixed IP.

issues.title: Zone 2 on/off appears inverted
issues.symptom: Zone 2 speakers play when Zone 2 shows off; no independent Zone 2 volume (TSR-7850).
issues.fix: Choose a '+Zone 2' amp assignment with Zone 2 speakers on EXTRA SP and set unused surround backs to NONE.

onkyo.title: Onkyo, Pioneer and Integra AV receivers
c4: Setup > Hardware > Network Standby > On (needed to power on over IP).
Setup > Hardware > HDMI CEC > Off. Onkyo's own note says set it Off if you see abnormal behaviour.
Setup > Hardware > Auto Standby > Off (otherwise it sleeps after 20 minutes with no input).
HDMI Standby Through: leave on Auto or Off to taste; with CEC Off you can choose Off.
DHCP reservation, wired. Menu names are from the TX-NR7100; other models may differ.

HDMI Standby Through: leave on Auto or Off to taste; with CEC Off you can choose Off.
DHCP reservation, wired. Menu names are from the TX-NR7100; other models may differ.

issues.title: Network Standby off or disabled automatically
issues.symptom: AVR won't power on over IP, or sleeps on its own.
issues.fix: Setup > Power Management (or Hardware) > Network Standby > On, and Auto Standby > Off.
issues.detail: Onkyo warns Network Standby may be disabled automatically if the network drops; then only the remote/front panel can power it on.

issues.title: Driver offline when the AVR is in standby
issues.symptom: TX-RZ900 shows offline when the room is off and won't turn on from Control4.
issues.fix: Confirm Network Standby is On and reserve the AVR's MAC on the router.
issues.detail: Unresolved in the thread.

issues.title: Pioneer/Onkyo network control drops every few weeks
issues.symptom: AVR drops off the network every couple of weeks; power cycle restores it.
issues.fix: Control it by RS-232 (3.5mm-to-DB9 from the controller).
issues.detail: Also update firmware by USB rather than network. On some units network and serial share a board.

issues.title: Room Off doesn't put the AVR in standby
issues.symptom: TX-NR3008 stays on after Room Off.
issues.fix: Check no other zone is still on.
issues.detail: Unresolved; serial driver only helped for a day.

issues.title: RS-232 ignored while the AVR is also networked
issues.symptom: Integra DRX-4 didn't respond on serial while still on the LAN.
issues.fix: Change the control binding in Composer from IP to serial (unplugging the network cable also made it work).

issues.title: CEC/ARC fights Control4
issues.symptom: Devices switch power or inputs by themselves with CEC on for ARC.
issues.fix: Run optical from TV to AVR for TV audio and disable CEC and ARC on both.
issues.detail: Atmos from TV apps needs eARC, so weigh this.

roku.title: Roku
c4: Network access: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > Control by mobile apps (External control) > Network access > Default or Enabled (not Limited or Disabled). Control4 stops working when this is Limited.
Roku firmware updates have reset this to Limited (14.6.4, July 2025). Re-check after updates.
If control still fails, unplug the Roku for 2 to 3 minutes.
DHCP reservation. Control by app needs the controller on the same network.
Unverified, check on the model: Settings > System > Power > Fast TV start On (Roku TVs) so it wakes over the network; turn HDMI-CEC (Settings > System > Control other devices) off.

tasks.text: Network access: Settings > System > Advanced system settings > Control by mobile apps (External control) > Network access > Default or Enabled (not Limited or Disabled). Control4 stops working when this is Limited.
Roku firmware updates have reset this to Limited (14.6.4, July 2025). Re-check after updates.
If control still fails, unplug the Roku for 2 to 3 minutes.
DHCP reservation. Control by app needs the controller on the same network.
Settings > System > Power > Fast TV start On (Roku TVs) so it wakes over the network; turn HDMI-CEC (Settings > System > Control other devices) off.

issues.title: Roku OS 14.1+ sets Network Access to Limited
issues.symptom: After a Roku update the Control4 driver stops controlling it (all control systems).
issues.fix: Settings > System > Advanced System Settings > Control by Mobile Apps > Network Access > Enabled, accept the warning, then power-cycle the Roku for 2-3 minutes.
issues.detail: Roku ECP docs: from 14.1 keypresses need Enabled. Updates can revert it; one user needed a factory reset.

issues.title: Control lost again after OS 14.6.4 (July 2025)
issues.symptom: Control4 control stopped while the Roku app still worked.
issues.fix: Set Network access to Enabled or Permissive (it had reverted to Limited).
issues.detail: One Ultra only worked on Permissive.

issues.title: UK menu wording differs
issues.symptom: UK installers can't find 'Control by mobile apps'.
issues.fix: UK path: Home > Settings > System > Advanced system settings > External Control > Network access > Default or Permissive (not Disable).

issues.title: Changing the setting on a racked Roku
issues.symptom: A rack Roku has no screen, so the setting can't be changed after an update breaks control.
issues.fix: Change it from the Roku mobile app on the same network, or plug the Roku into a temporary TV.
issues.detail: Consider an IR driver as a backup.

issues.title: Driver can't find Rokus on rescan
issues.symptom: Rokus stop responding and rescan doesn't find them.
issues.fix: Enter the Roku's IP in the driver properties (with a DHCP reservation) and give each Roku a unique name.
issues.detail: Identical names caused failures; 8 posters confirmed.

issues.title: ECP port 8060 and SSDP across VLANs
issues.symptom: Roku reachable but the driver can't discover or control it across VLANs/firewalls.
issues.fix: Allow TCP 8060 from controller to Roku and SSDP 239.255.255.250:1900; test by browsing to http://roku-ip:8060.

issues.title: Roku TV can't be woken from deep standby
issues.symptom: A Roku TV in low-power standby doesn't answer SSDP, so IP can't wake it.
issues.fix: Keep IR as the power-on fallback for Roku TVs.

issues.title: Mini apps launch but no navigation
issues.symptom: Control4 mini apps launch on the Roku but navigation doesn't work afterwards.
issues.fix: Check the room's audio bindings from the Roku to the audio endpoint; if that fails, turn off pass-through in device properties.

issues.title: Roku CEC vs Control4
issues.symptom: With CEC on, the Roku and other devices change power or inputs themselves.
issues.fix: Disable CEC on the Roku and the display.

sonos.title: Sonos
c4: Give every player a DHCP reservation. Sonos uses SDDP with Control4, so the driver follows IP changes, but reservations still avoid trouble.
Control4 forum experience: almost all Sonos/Control4 issues come from network design (multicast, STP, mesh/Wi-Fi). Wire players or a single SonosNet root where you can.
Arc/Beam/Ray on TV: they use HDMI-CEC/eARC for TV audio, so keep CEC on for that TV input only if the Sonos is the TV's sound.

tasks.text: Give every player a DHCP reservation. Sonos uses SDDP with Control4, so the driver follows IP changes, but reservations still avoid trouble.
Control4 forum experience: almost all Sonos/Control4 issues come from network design (multicast, STP, mesh/Wi-Fi). Wire players or a single SonosNet root where you can.
Arc/Beam/Ray on TV: they use HDMI-CEC/eARC for TV audio, so keep CEC on for that TV input only if the Sonos is the TV's sound.

issues.title: Jan 2025 volume drops to zero
issues.symptom: Sonos volume jumps to 0 when controlled from Control4.
issues.fix: Update Sonos players to the latest firmware (Control4 fix rolled out automatically).
issues.detail: Sonos staff confirmed; resolved.

issues.title: Use the current Sonos driver set
issues.symptom: Missing features, or players lost after IP changes.
issues.fix: Use the current drivers: Sonos (sonos.c4z), Sonos Network and Sonos Global Line In.
issues.detail: SDDP on TCP 1400 (main driver only). Min OS 2.8.2.

issues.title: STP on managed switches
issues.symptom: Wired or mixed wired/SonosNet players drop out or loop on managed switches.
issues.fix: Enable STP with the main switch at bridge priority 4096 and Sonos ports as edge ports (BPDU Guard and Root Guard off).
issues.detail: Sonos STP article. Use STP not RSTP for hybrid wired/SonosNet, and prefer all-wired or all-wireless.

issues.title: Multicast/IGMP on managed Wi-Fi
issues.symptom: Discovery and control unreliable on managed Wi-Fi.
issues.fix: Enable IGMP snooping on the Sonos LAN and turn off multicast-to-unicast and multicast filtering on the Sonos SSID.
issues.detail: Keep all Sonos on one subnet, never a guest network.

issues.title: Reserve IPs for bonded surrounds
issues.symptom: Bonded surrounds on SonosNet drop out of the router's DHCP/ARP tables; random disconnects.
issues.fix: Make a DHCP reservation for every Sonos unit, including surrounds and subs.
issues.detail: Disputed; some run fine without.

issues.title: Arc keeps playing after Room Off
issues.symptom: Room Off turns the projector off but the Arc and Sub keep playing.
issues.fix: Check bindings so the Sonos driver has a valid audio output path (or a dummy audio connection).
issues.detail: Matrix kept sending audio, so the Arc stayed on input. Not confirmed fixed.

issues.title: Can't group while the Arc is in Watch
issues.symptom: While the Arc is in Watch, other Sonos rooms aren't offered for grouping in Control4.
issues.fix: Group from the Sonos app meanwhile and report it to Control4.

issues.title: Connect volume jumps to 0 or 100% after OS upgrade
issues.symptom: After Core3 and OS 3.4.3, Connects on pass-through jump to 0% or 100%.
issues.fix: Update Sonos and Control4 firmware and raise it with Control4 support.

issues.title: Driver limits to explain to the client
issues.symptom: 50 favourites limit, no 'is playing' conditionals, no line-in switching (breaks doorbell announcements).
issues.fix: Use the Sonos Global Line In driver for line-in sources and set expectations with the client.

issues.title: Port line-in lag as TV audio endpoint
issues.symptom: TV audio through a Port line-in lags the picture by seconds.
issues.fix: Set the line-in Audio Delay to minimum (~75 ms) on the Port with the line-in, and wire the Ports.

pjlink.title: PJLink projectors (Epson, Panasonic, NEC and others)
c4: Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink > On.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink Password: set one (up to 32 alphanumeric, @ allowed) and enter it in the Control4 driver.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > Control4 SDDP > On.
Epson: Extended > Standby Mode > Communication On, so it answers over the network in standby. Some models need A/V Output set to While Projecting and Auto Power On Off first.
NEC: projectors can cut LAN power after 3 minutes without traffic (EuP). Set standby so the LAN stays alive. On some models use the Expert menu: Setup > Expert > Standby mode setting > Disable.
Unverified, check on the model: Panasonic: Setup > Standby mode > Normal (not Eco), Network > PJLink on.
DHCP reservation or static IP. PJLink is TCP 4352.

installer.title: NEC Expert menu
steps: On the NEC remote press Help, Up, Left, Help.
Press Menu. EXPERT shows in the bottom right corner.
Setup > Expert (or Expert2) > Standby mode setting > Disable.

tasks.text: Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink > On.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > PJLink Password: set one (up to 32 alphanumeric, @ allowed) and enter it in the Control4 driver.
Epson: Network > Projector Control > Control4 SDDP > On.
Epson: Extended > Standby Mode > Communication On, so it answers over the network in standby. Some models need A/V Output set to While Projecting and Auto Power On Off first.
NEC: projectors can cut LAN power after 3 minutes without traffic (EuP). Set standby so the LAN stays alive. On some models use the Expert menu: Setup > Expert > Standby mode setting > Disable.
Panasonic: Setup > Standby mode > Normal (not Eco), Network > PJLink on.
DHCP reservation or static IP. PJLink is TCP 4352.

issues.title: Epson: IP power-on needs Standby Mode 'Communication On'
issues.symptom: IP control is lost once the projector is off and Control4 can't turn it back on.
issues.fix: Set Standby Mode > Communication On (Operation or Extended menu), and where present set Priority Control Interface to the LAN port in use.
issues.detail: Chowmain's Epson Universal driver lists it as required. Epson: wired LAN stops responding if the link is lost for over 15 minutes.

issues.title: Epson LS12000 stops responding to IP power after 1-2 weeks
issues.symptom: With Epson's certified IP driver the projector works for 1-2 weeks then ignores power until unplugged.
issues.fix: Set the monitor password on both the projector and the driver (Epson support's advice).
issues.detail: If it still locks up, posters used a driver without authentication and disabled authentication on the projector. Same thread: EDID black screens at power-on fixed with an EDID manager.

issues.title: Projector misses on/off or powers on and off by itself
issues.symptom: An Epson misses most power-ons and half of Room Offs, and switches on or off by itself.
issues.fix: Disable HDMI-CEC on sources, AVR and projector (including the projector's receiver-control option).
issues.detail: Also slow or disable driver polling (30 s polling queued tens of thousands of commands for one poster) and add ~10 s before the off command. Check long passive RS232-over-RJ45 runs.

issues.title: Commands lost during warm-up or cool-down
issues.symptom: An input command sent right after power-on is lost; commands blocked while cooling.
issues.fix: Use a two-way IP driver that waits for confirmed power-on before sending the input, or add a Composer Delay before the input command.
issues.detail: Chowmain PJLink driver polls every 5 s during power transitions.

issues.title: Screen drops 2 minutes late
issues.symptom: Motorised screen drops about 2 minutes after projector power-on and raises 2 minutes after Room Off.
issues.fix: Trigger the screen from the room's power state or video selection change, not from the projector's power event.
issues.detail: Control4 marks the projector On only after warm-up completes.

issues.title: NEC: LAN port sleeps in standby (EuP)
issues.symptom: LAN (and probably HDBaseT) control is lost after the projector idles in standby.
issues.fix: Use SLEEP standby, or in the Expert menu (Help, Up, Left, Help, then Menu) set Setup > Expert > Standby mode setting > Disable.
issues.detail: LAN can switch off after 180 s with no traffic.

issues.title: Panasonic: Standby mode ECO disables network control
issues.symptom: The projector can't be powered on over IP.
issues.fix: Set Projector Setup > Eco Management > Standby Mode > Normal.
issues.detail: Near 0 °C warm-up can take ~5 minutes. Source is a pro (PT-RZ575) manual.

issues.title: Panasonic: protect mode needs an MD5 hash
issues.symptom: Control system shows connected but commands do nothing; projector asks for a 32-byte hash.
issues.fix: Use a driver that supports the password hash, or set non-protect mode (web control as admin, save with blank password fields).
issues.detail: Atlona KB; applies to any controller whose driver lacks the hash.

issues.title: PJLink ERRA / ERR3 errors
issues.symptom: Commands fail with ERRA (auth error) or ERR3 (unavailable time, e.g. in standby).
issues.fix: Enter the exact PJLink password in the driver (or disable PJLink auth if the driver can't), and only send non-power commands once the projector reports On.
issues.detail: PJLink auth is MD5 of password + projector's random number; sessions close after 30 s.

issues.title: HDMI handshake black screen at power-up
issues.symptom: Intermittent black screen or no audio after Control4 powers the chain (projector, processor, AVR).
issues.fix: Power the projector last, with a power-on delay in the other devices' drivers.
issues.detail: A trigger that power-cycled the processor whenever the projector came on caused an endless loop.

jvc.title: JVC D-ILA projectors
c4: Function > ECO Mode > Off. With it On, JVC says RS-232C and LAN control can't be used in standby.
Function > Network: set DHCP Client Off and enter a static IP (or keep DHCP with a reservation), then Set.
Function > Control4 SDDP > On.
Function > Network Password: 8 to 10 characters. Any third-party IP control system (Control4) must be given this password.
Unverified, check on the model: IP control port is TCP 20554 (JVC 'PJ_OK / PJREQ / PJACK' handshake).

tasks.text: Function > ECO Mode > Off. With it On, JVC says RS-232C and LAN control can't be used in standby.
Function > Network: set DHCP Client Off and enter a static IP (or keep DHCP with a reservation), then Set.
Function > Control4 SDDP > On.
Function > Network Password: 8 to 10 characters. Any third-party IP control system (Control4) must be given this password.
IP control port is TCP 20554 (JVC 'PJ_OK / PJREQ / PJACK' handshake).

issues.title: 2024+ models (NZ900/NZ800/RS4200/RS3200) don't work with older JVC drivers
issues.symptom: An NZ9/RS4100 driver loads in Composer but an NZ900/RS4200 doesn't respond.
issues.fix: Use the model-specific Control4 driver for DLA-NZ900/NZ800/RS4200/RS3200 (listed on the Control4 tech support blog), not the NZ9 driver.
issues.detail: JVC changed the handshake password from plain text to a SHA-256 hash (password + 'JVCKWPJ', no trailing space). No c4forums poster confirmed a fix.

issues.title: Network password must be set before IP control works
issues.symptom: The projector doesn't accept LAN control.
issues.fix: Set Function > Network > Network Password (8-10 characters) on the projector and enter the same password in the driver.
issues.detail: Control port TCP 20554 (Home Assistant JVC integration doc).

issues.title: ECO Mode On kills LAN control in standby
issues.symptom: Control4 can't power the projector on from standby; all indicators off.
issues.fix: Set Function > ECO Mode > Off.
issues.detail: With ECO On the projector also goes to standby after 15 minutes with no signal.

issues.title: Lens memory over IP: use Installation Modes
issues.symptom: Lens memory IR codes from older models don't carry over, and the IP driver has no lens-memory command.
issues.fix: Store each aspect/lens position in Installation Mode 1-10 and call that mode from a Control4 custom button.
issues.detail: Installation Modes also store other settings. Confirmed on an NX5.

issues.title: Driver flips online/offline and ignores power
issues.symptom: With the 2016-era Control4 JVC IP driver the projector flips online/offline and ignores power while 'offline', though ping never drops.
issues.fix: Go back to the older JVC IP driver (the command set is unchanged).
issues.detail: 2 posters on OS 2.8.x; no official fix.

issues.title: Power off ignored just after warm-up; polling closes menus
issues.symptom: An off sent just after power-on is ignored, and on-screen menus vanish while the driver polls.
issues.fix: Don't send power off within about 30 s of the projector reaching On, and pause polling while someone is in the menus.
issues.detail: From RTI's JVC driver doc.

issues.title: NZ9/RS4100 won't power on through Control4 after firmware 2.0
issues.symptom: After firmware 2.0 the projector won't power on from Control4.
issues.fix: Power down fully, unplug for about a minute, then restart.
issues.detail: Advice to disconnect HDMI during the ~1 hour update is unverified hearsay. No confirmed fix.

appletv.title: Apple TV
c4: Control4 guide: Settings > General > Sleep After > Never.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > On.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > Room: set the right room.
Control4 guide: set up with the customer's Apple ID using 'Set Up with Device', on tvOS 12.1 or later.
Control4 guide: after choosing the Apple TV in the driver, restart it (Settings > System > Restart) and check the driver shows 'Remote Activated'.
Settings > Remotes and Devices > Control TVs and Receivers > Off, so the Apple TV doesn't turn the TV on or switch inputs over CEC.

'Cinema mode' most likely means Match Content: Settings > Video and Audio > Match Content > Match Dynamic Range and Match Frame Rate. With these on the TV blanks for a moment when content starts, which looks like a fault on a matrix/Control4 system. Turn them off if that's a problem.
Other candidates: Settings > Video and Audio > Reduce Loud Sounds (night mode) Off, and the TV's own picture mode (Cinema/Filmmaker), which is a TV setting, not Apple TV.
Wire it (Ethernet) and give it a DHCP reservation.

tasks.text: Control4 guide: Settings > General > Sleep After > Never.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > On.
Control4 guide: Settings > AirPlay > Room: set the right room.
Control4 guide: set up with the customer's Apple ID using 'Set Up with Device', on tvOS 12.1 or later.
Control4 guide: after choosing the Apple TV in the driver, restart it (Settings > System > Restart) and check the driver shows 'Remote Activated'.
Settings > Remotes and Devices > Control TVs and Receivers > Off, so the Apple TV doesn't turn the TV on or switch inputs over CEC.

'Cinema mode' most likely means Match Content: Settings > Video and Audio > Match Content > Match Dynamic Range and Match Frame Rate. With these on the TV blanks for a moment when content starts, which looks like a fault on a matrix/Control4 system. Turn them off if that's a problem.
Other candidates: Settings > Video and Audio > Reduce Loud Sounds (night mode) Off, and the TV's own picture mode (Cinema/Filmmaker), which is a TV setting, not Apple TV.
Wire it (Ethernet) and give it a DHCP reservation.

issues.title: tvOS 18 broke Control4 IP control
issues.symptom: Apple TVs on tvOS 18 stopped responding to Control4 remotes and touchscreens; Halo voice failed too.
issues.fix: Update every Apple TV to tvOS 18.4 or later, with Apple Bridge driver v78+ and Voice Coordinator v120+.
issues.detail: Snap One status: IP fixed in tvOS 18.2 (Dec 2024), voice in 18.4 (Apr 2025). Snap One advised holding tvOS upgrades during incidents.

issues.title: Bind IR too, for automatic failover
issues.symptom: Apple TV becomes uncontrollable whenever IP/HomeKit control drops.
issues.fix: Use the current Control4 Apple TV IP driver and also wire and bind an IR emitter; the driver fails over to IR.
issues.detail: Halo voice still needs IP.

issues.title: HC-series controllers can't run the IP driver
issues.symptom: After a tvOS update an HC800 system loses Apple TV control.
issues.fix: Use the IR Apple TV driver on HC controllers, or upgrade to an EA/CA controller for IP.
issues.detail: IP driver needs EA-series or CA-10 and OS 2.10.6+.

issues.title: Control lost after an Apple Home update or HomeKit change
issues.symptom: Control4 controls the TV and AVR but not the Apple TV; reboots don't help.
issues.fix: In Composer run Apple Bridge > Actions > Refresh, then in the Control4 app turn Apple TV Control on and re-add the Control4 bridge in Apple Home.
issues.detail: One poster runs the Bridge Refresh from startup programming. OS 3.3.0.

issues.title: Sudden loss after Apple Bridge driver update
issues.symptom: Apple TV shows 'Control4 Remote Connected' but ignores the remote.
issues.fix: Reboot the Control4 controller.
issues.detail: Fixed it for 2 posters after a 2021 bridge update.

issues.title: Driver offline or room blank
issues.symptom: Apple TV driver offline in Composer, or its selector/room is blank.
issues.fix: On the Apple TV remove the AirPlay and HomeKit room, power cycle, reselect the room, then reselect it in the driver.
issues.detail: Also check iCloud uses the same Apple ID as the Home app. Dealer support article.

issues.title: 'Unable to complete Apple TV integration'
issues.symptom: The Control4 app fails to enable Apple TV Control, or only some Apple TVs appear.
issues.fix: Make sure the Control4 account email matches the Apple ID used for Home, then toggle Apple TV Control off and on.
issues.detail: Also: DHCP reservation, hardwire at least one Apple TV, update iOS/tvOS, check for a stale hub in HomeKit. Nothing independently confirmed; some gave up and used IR.

issues.title: Apple ID password change breaks IP control
issues.symptom: After an Apple ID password change, Apple TVs stop responding to IP control.
issues.fix: Update the credentials on every Apple TV, then remove and re-add the Control4 bridge in Apple Home.
issues.detail: Fixed 7 of 8 units in the thread.

issues.title: Siri Remote volume fights Control4 volume
issues.symptom: The Siri Remote changes TV/AVR volume outside Control4.
issues.fix: Settings > Remotes and Devices > Volume Control: set Off, or match how Control4 drives the AVR (Receiver via IR / Learn New Device).
issues.detail: Options: Auto, HDMI, Receiver via IR, TV via IR, Off, Learn New Device.

issues.title: Third-party driver without HomeKit
issues.symptom: HomeKit / Apple Bridge pairing keeps breaking.
issues.fix: Consider Intrinsic Dev's Apple TV IP driver, which needs no HomeKit pairing.
issues.detail: Uses Apple's unofficial protocol, so it's tvOS-version dependent (separate tvOS 16+ driver).

all_tasks.text: Give every controlled device a DHCP reservation (or static IP outside the pool) before adding it in Composer.
Wire it if it has an Ethernet port. Several TVs only wake over LAN (Wake-on-LAN) when wired.
Turn HDMI-CEC off on TVs, AVRs and sources unless the driver needs it. CEC fights the control system (inputs and power changing on their own).
Set network/IP standby to the 'always on' option so the device can be turned on over IP. It uses a little more standby power.
Turn off eco / auto power off / auto standby timers so devices don't sleep or drop off the network behind Control4's back.
Turn on Control4 SDDP where the device offers it (Epson, JVC, LG, Sonos) so the driver follows IP changes.
Note the MAC address and any pairing key or password in the site network map, never in the driver notes.
After a firmware update, re-check these settings. Updates have reset them before (Roku network access, Samsung pairing).

task_note: Each tasks[] item is one action with a stable id (device-key.slug). Ids never change once published; new items get new ids, removed items are dropped. Link a task to a device by site + device IP/MAC + id. verified=false means forum or general knowledge, check on the model.
issues_note: devices.key.issues[] are known problems from forums and vendor notes, each {id, title, symptom, fix, detail, evidence, sources}. evidence: vendor = manufacturer/Control4/driver vendor doc, forum-multiple = 2+ independent posters, forum-single = one report. Ids are stable like task ids.
